title: [22/7/2023] Water levels of 6 cities in Australia
prompt: The chart below shows the water levels of 6 cities in Australia in October 2009 and 2010. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the water reservoir levels as percentages of their maximum capacity in six Australian cities in October of 2009 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, most cities witnessed an increase in their water storage over the one-year period, with the exception of Darwin, which experienced a decline. Additionally, Canberra not only maintained the highest reservoir level but also showed the most significant rise among all cities.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at cities with higher water reserves, Sydney and Canberra both recorded figures of approximately 75% in 2009, whereas Brisbane's reservoirs were about 55% full. By 2010, despite Brisbane's water level remaining stable, Sydney saw a modest increase to 81%, and Canberra experienced a substantial rise to 98% of its maximum volume.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining cities, Darwin and Perth had relatively similar water levels in 2009, at around 44% and 40% respectively, while Melbourne had the lowest initial level at 25%. In contrast to Perth's level rising significantly to 61% in the following year, Darwin's figure fell to approximately 28%. Meanwhile, Melbourne saw its water level increase considerably to 38% by the end of the period.
